title: Stoics on the soul's duration; Cleanthes and Chrysippus; Pliny impiously mocks immortality
pass_a_gloss: Pliny, a philosopher not belonging toward better mark, in Natural History book 7, chapter 33, impiously mocks the sentence on the immortality belonging toward souls: Those, he says, stand as inventions belonging toward childish deliriums and belonging toward a greed never to cease from mortality. Cleanthes held that all remain until the conflagration; but Chrysippus only those belonging toward the wise. The same Stoics, according toward Diogenes Laertius book 6 on Zeno, hold the soul twice-begotten with generation.
pass_b_english: The same Stoics, according to Diogenes Laertius book 6 on Zeno, [hold the soul] twice-begotten with generation. Cleanthes held that all remain until the conflagration; but Chrysippus only those of the wise. Pliny, a philosopher not of better mark, in Natural History book 7, chapter 33, impiously mocks the sentence on the immortality of souls: Those, he says, are inventions of childish deliriums and of a greed never to cease from mortality.
source_text: Iidem apud Diogenem Laertium lib. 6. in Zenone, animam bis cum genitam. Cleanthes omnes permanere statuit usque ad conflagrationem: Chrysippus vero solas sapientum. Plinius non probioris notae philosophus lib. 7. c. 33. sententiam de immortalitate animarum impie ridet: Puerilium, inquiens, ista deliramentorum avidaeque nunquam desinere mortalitatis commenta sunt.
